name: stats
title: Statistics with R
summary: R with mixed models, survival analysis, meta-analysis and the tidyverse basics; PyMC for Bayesian models; panel-data econometrics and survival analysis in Python.

tools.name: R
tools.does: the R language for statistics; scripts run with Rscript and save plots to files

tools.name: lme4 and nlme
tools.usage: R: library(lme4); lmer(y ~ x + (1 | group), data)
tools.check: Rscript -e 'suppressMessages(library(lme4)); m <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), sleepstudy); cat("days", round(fixef(m)[2], 2), "\n")'

tools.name: survival
tools.does: survival analysis in R: Kaplan-Meier, Cox models
tools.usage: R: library(survival); coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ x, data)
tools.check: Rscript -e 'library(survival); m <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age, lung); cat("age", round(coef(m), 4), "\n")'

tools.name: metafor
tools.does: meta-analysis in R: pooled effects, heterogeneity, funnel plots
tools.usage: R: library(metafor); rma(yi, vi, data = dat)
tools.check: Rscript -e 'suppressMessages(library(metafor)); d <- escalc(measure="RR", ai=tpos, bi=tneg, ci=cpos, di=cneg, data=dat.bcg); cat("pooled", round(coef(rma(yi, vi, data=d)), 3), "\n")'

tools.name: R data packages
tools.does: data handling and plots in R: data.table, dplyr, tidyr, readr, ggplot2; robust standard errors with sandwich and lmtest; mgcv, car, emmeans, boot
tools.check: Rscript -e 'suppressMessages({library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(data.table); library(sandwich); library(lmtest); library(mgcv); library(car); library(emmeans)}); cat("packages ok\n")'

tools.name: pymc
tools.does: Bayesian models with MCMC sampling in Python; ArviZ for diagnostics. The first run of a model compiles it, which takes a minute
tools.usage: python: import pymc as pm, arviz as az

tools.name: lifelines
tools.usage: python: from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter
tools.check: python -c "from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter as K; k=K().fit([1,2,3,4],[1,1,0,1]); print('median', k.median_survival_time_)"

tools.name: linearmodels and pingouin
tools.does: panel-data and instrumental-variable regression (linearmodels); common tests and effect sizes (pingouin)
tools.usage: python: from linearmodels.panel import PanelOLS; import pingouin
